key_insight: A hybrid GNP/C60 epoxy coating plus CNT surface treatment substantially improved adhesion, durability, barrier protection, and water-repellent behavior on HVOF-metallized CFRP.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers a practical route to extend the service life and environmental resistance of thermally sprayed CFRP metalized surfaces in harsh mechanical and corrosive settings.
method: Applied a graphene nanoplatelet/fullerene C60 reinforced epoxy over HVOF-metallized CFRP.
Used CNT-based surface modification to tailor wettability and ice behavior.
Evaluated morphology, adhesion, wear, and electrochemical barrier performance.
evidence_signal: Pull-off strength rose from 320 to 650 psi, tensile strength increased from about 25 to 56 MPa, mass loss dropped by over 50%, and water contact angle exceeded 155° after CNT treatment.
watch_item: Results are based on laboratory-scale tests, so coating uniformity, scalability, and long-term field durability still need validation.
paper_title: Hybrid Graphene Nanoplatelet/C60 Nanocomposite Modification of HVOF-Metallized Carbon Fiber-Reinforced Polymer Coatings to Improve Adhesion, Barrier Performance, and Surface Functionality
